3: See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
4: non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
5: independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.
6: 
7: The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
8: in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
9: proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
18: data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
19: competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.
20: 
21: > **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.
22: 
23: **WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. Models, vendors, runtimes and human operators may change; the durable record, authority boundary, provenance and correction mechanisms carry the work forward. Research is the first application running on that structure.
24: 
25: In everyday terms: WAKE keeps the record, gives a model a bounded view of it,
26: checks the model's suggestion against rules, and records what happened. A model
27: never writes directly to the database.
28: 
29: The [wake metaphor](why-wake.md) connects this lifecycle to persistent
30: consequences: proposals express possibilities, governance evaluates them, and
31: accepted transitions change governed state. Rejected proposals leave receipts
32: without becoming accepted transitions; deferrals and provider failures have
33: their own recorded outcomes. The record supplies bounded context for subsequent
34: work without granting the next model authority. This is a conceptual reading of
35: the lifecycle; the technical guarantees below come from the kernel, application
36: policy and runtime contracts, not from quantum physics.
43:   end
44:   topics --> K[WAKE kernel]
45:   evidence --> K
46:   K --> record[(One durable record)]
47:   model[Replaceable model] -->|suggestion| K
48:   K -->|bounded context| model
49:   deploy[Container or Codespace runtime] --> K
50:   views[Website and Console views] -. read-only views .-> record
51: ```
52: 
53: **What this means:** the application decides what work is allowed, the kernel
54: records and checks transitions, and each node owns one authoritative record. A
55: website or Console is a view of records, not another source of truth.
56: 
57: Research-topic configuration can classify experimental seeds and name their
58: experiment. Existing charter/topic-change events retain configuration fingerprints,
59: activation times, node/runtime/provider settings and accepted-version boundaries.
61: Verified startup adopts trusted configuration changes before the first export,
62: including on restored nodes waiting for quota. This appends the normal topic-change
63: boundary without resetting accepted-cycle versions or waiting for inference.
64: An explicitly authorized complete installation reset instead creates new records
65: and identity; it is not replay, migration or an authority merge. See the
66: [research expansion](research-expansion.md). Model-formulated questions remain
67: ordinary governed project/reframe actions, never configuration edits.
